_about: Edward Polhill (1622-1694?) of Burwash, Sussex, a lay Calvinist theologian: The Divine Will Considered in its Eternal Decrees and Holy Execution of them (London, 1673); Precious Faith Considered in its Nature, Working and Growth (London, 1675); Speculum Theologiae in Christo (London, 1678); Armatura Dei, or a Preparation for Suffering (London: Thomas Cockerill; catalogued 1682, the OCR of the imprint reads 1692); Christus in Corde, or the Mystical Union between Christ and Believers, third edition, ed. Thomas Cloutt (London: Holdsworth, 1823); and the Essay on the Extent of the Death of Christ, from the Divine Will (Berwick: Thomas Melrose, 1842). The 17th-century books are EEBO scans except the Speculum, which is Princeton's copy. Internet Archive OCR, raw and unconverted; each title page read before listing.

polhill-divine-will-1673.author: The OCR breaks the name: the title page reads 'By Eowand Poraiis of[ Burwash] in Sussex Esquire', 1673; Precious Faith (1675) names him 'Edward Polhill of Burwash in Sussex, Esq.'

polhill-speculum-theologiae-1678.author: The OCR breaks the name: the title page reads 'By EDWARD POLE ILL of Bmwafi in Sujfex, Efq', printed for Tho. Cockerill, 1678, Polhill's publisher for Precious Faith and Armatura Dei.
